failure_modes.title: Over-approval from partial-match on shared head-noun without validating qualifier-clause
failure_modes.symptom: L over-approved links where a sentence contains a multi-word-phrase whose head-noun partially matches a candidate, but the surrounding qualifier-clause or modifier does not support that candidate.
failure_modes.apparent_cause: The current bank is empty, so there is no validation rule requiring exact-match or compatible modifier structure before approval. This allows a shared head-noun to propagate a link across distinct multi-word-phrase variants.
failure_modes.suggested_direction: Add a validation pattern that under-rejects less and over-approves less by checking whether a partial-match is licensed by matching modifier, possessive, or qualifier-clause context. If only the head-noun matches and the modifier differs, block approval unless another supporting cue exists.
failure_modes.abstract_example_pair:
TP: A sentence names the multi-word-phrase "alpha unit" in subject-position, and the candidate is the exact-match "alpha unit".
FP: A sentence names the multi-word-phrase "beta unit" inside a qualifier-clause, and L links it to the candidate "alpha unit" only because of the shared head-noun "unit".

failure_modes.title: Container-of or sub-element-of mention mistaken for direct mention
failure_modes.symptom: L over-approved a candidate when the sentence appears to mention a related container-of or sub-element-of expression rather than the candidate itself.
failure_modes.apparent_cause: Without judge rules distinguishing direct mention from related structure, any nearby partial-match or namespace-prefix overlap can be treated as sufficient evidence for the candidate.
failure_modes.suggested_direction: Add judge rules that separate direct exact-match mentions from container-of and sub-element-of mentions. Require explicit support when a sentence refers to a larger container or a nested sub-element rather than the candidate head-noun itself.
failure_modes.abstract_example_pair:
TP: The sentence states, "The gamma element performs the check," where "gamma element" is the exact-match candidate.
FP: The sentence states, "The gamma element's delta part performs the check," and L links the sentence to "gamma element" even though the predicate is attached to the sub-element-of expression.

failure_modes.title: Alias-of ambiguity not constrained by local discourse cues
failure_modes.symptom: L over-approved a candidate because a short form, namespace-prefix, or reduced multi-word-phrase was treated as alias-of the candidate without enough local evidence.
failure_modes.apparent_cause: The current bank has no seed disambiguation rules, so abbreviated or reduced forms can be propagated to the wrong candidate when multiple candidates share a partial-match surface form.
failure_modes.suggested_direction: Add disambiguation patterns that require local antecedent support, apposition, parenthetical introduction, or exact-match establishment before treating a reduced form as alias-of a candidate.
failure_modes.abstract_example_pair:
TP: "The alpha module (AM) stores state. AM also emits updates." The parenthetical establishes alias-of, so the later reduced form is valid.
FP: "The module emits updates." L links "module" to "alpha module" even though no antecedent, apposition, or parenthetical established that alias-of relation.
